summary: the writ is read; the deputy is named; the auditor reveals himself
the avatar reviews what Act 1-2 choices bought and cost; ascension_signals' hidden telemetry (sig_defection_handling, sig_kest_restitution) starts reading here, invisibly
the deposed patrons fall; no one strikes down the Enlightened One himself; the avatar watches a true good ending still cost the plurality something
the avatar faces him directly; the Idol's shape is unmistakably the Hierophant's colossus too; victory reads as exposure, not martyrdom
the defense scenario ends in capture, not a kill; Methodios watches his claimant taken alive, and says nothing yet
the Diadem convenes at Kaisareia; the avatar (or whoever holds the relevant commission) recommends sentence; SETS flag_hierophant_verdict (mercy | execution), forking to ch_h33_mercy or ch_h34_war1
Methodios reframes the capitulation as a hidden necessary descent, not a defeat; the movement goes to ground; a second battle is already forming
the first fractured region takes up arms; a former ally's banner now marks an enemy den
a second front opens; the avatar counts what the sentence chosen at Kaisareia is actually costing, region by region
the war's last field; Methodios names the killing a betrayal, not a verdict, and means it

Macuil offers both explanations for the drowned valley -- divine judgment on the old seat, or the ground simply dropping, per rgn_drowned_march's own explanation_sacred/explanation_material -- and refuses to say which one is true; 'the north wind winds' reads as much like weather passing over an unanswered question as it does a location. 'Dark in some runs' (this sect's own doctrine language, reused the way sc_p_indech's summary reuses it for sect_coast) reads off flag_deaths: a costly run hears his silence as an indictment, a clean one hears it as genuine refusal to judge -- same words either way, matching sect_march's own wild cosmology just as closely as the earlier, wrong-region draft matched sect_coast's renunciation -- Macuil's personal refusal to adjudicate isn't itself sect doctrine, so the device transfers regardless of which sect actually claims the ground he stands on.

Indech's fisher cult reads the lake for an answer it may not actually contain -- same refusal-to-adjudicate as Macuil (teaches_system's shared line), here through water instead of stone; 'dark in some runs' (sects.sect_coast's own note, now applying to both its paralogues) reads off flag_deaths the same way sc_p_macuil's summary does: a costly crossing of the ford reads the cult's silence as an indictment, a clean one reads it as genuine renunciation, same words either way.

No hermit here to refuse an answer -- the Shadhavar doesn't judge, it lures, and named.nmd_shadhavar is explicit the lure is what it IS, not a performance: the song plays whether or not anyone is meant to hear it. The avatar reaches the lowest terrace already knowing capture is a category error for this one -- 'uncontrolled by design' (its own defection_trigger) means nothing here is actually decided by the player's approach, only witnessed.

The feather is not here to be picked up -- named.nmd_simurgh is explicit she 'answers whoever holds the feather', past tense already decided, and nothing in this chapter's own grounding gives the avatar one. She watches from the nest and does not descend; 'cleanses corruption... will not do it on request' reads as the same shape of refusal sect_march's own hermit gives two ridges over, gentler in tone but just as final.

No feather, no fisher cult, no refusal to judge -- the Karkadann's terms are the simplest of the Named's: it guards the doves, and nothing it has not decided to protect matters to it either way. named.nmd_karkadann's own notes call it 'the plain one on purpose', and the avatar leaves the clearing without a riddle to carry, just the doves, still there, still guarded, whether or not that was ever in question.

Visible from the moment you cross the edge -- 'a single figure legible at distance' (rgn_glass_flats' own texture) -- and no closer for it. named.nmd_anzu contracts with whoever can read the register, not whoever owns it or beats it; the avatar reaches the interior already unsure which of those the fight itself was ever supposed to prove.

Nothing lands. named.nmd_huma is explicit it never does -- 'cannot be owned, only flown under', and whatever unit its shadow crossed on the way east carries that the rest of the way, unasked and unrefusable. No fight for it, no pact, no register to sign -- sect_road's own doctrine ('the payment has already been made, on your behalf, and you were not consulted') describes the Huma's blessing as exactly as it describes their god's.

The shrine above was re-consecrated years ago -- 'complicit hands scrubbed from its stones' (map_v21's own note) -- and none of that touched what's down here. sect_vashti's own doctrine says a sacrament from complicit hands is void until re-made clean; the records in this room were never a sacrament, never re-made, and never once addressed by the reconsecration built directly over them. The avatar leaves with paper, not absolution -- those were always two different things, whatever the shrine upstairs implied.

Grain hits the quay under a crowd's own noise, and it's the opportunists working that noise, not the crowd itself, that the avatar's people end up fighting. The Diadem calls it protest management; the dockworkers call it Thursday.
Anthe's harbour sits two levels below the town and dry -- the same stranded-water scar that runs the length of this coast, here just a port trying to keep working above it.

The renunciants who live in this ruin don't fight and don't explain themselves either; the avatar's people clear scavengers off the middle terrace and leave them exactly as unbothered as they found them.
Nothing to hide behind and nowhere it would matter -- the dry country doesn't punish bad positioning so much as make the question irrelevant. Whoever moves faster decides the terms.

The road narrows where the lava fanned out and never fully cooled into anything wider than one cart. Local levies hold the narrows less because they can win there than because it's the only place worth holding at all.

The gate doesn't open and nobody inside answers a question -- sect_vashti's own seat living up to sects.sect_vashti's own note almost a decade before ch_v21 confirms it in writing: no talk conversations available on their seat map, Act 1 included.
No crowd at Halder, no cart to chase -- just a quiet trade in medicine nobody upriver wants to ask too many questions about, and opportunists who noticed the same thing the avatar's people did.
The bell tower shows itself for one dry season and vanishes back under for the next; whoever built the town underneath it clearly expected the water to stay put. It didn't.
Ostrova sits close enough to the Plains that the Assembly's own writ starts to feel optional past a certain point on the map -- the raiders who hit it clearly agree.
Downstream the rift filled and became a lake with a story about it. Up here it's still just a cliff, and holding the shelf along its edge has no story attached yet, only the fighting.
The canopy takes the sky away from anything that flies and leaves the ground fight exactly as it would be anywhere else -- bandits who know that difference use it.
New scripture arrives here the way it always does for sect_march -- dictated, in progress, never finished -- and the levies being talked into believing it were conscripts an hour ago.

Obedience belongs to the throne, and the chapel at Vetch says so with its gate shut rather than its doors open -- the same welcome ch_c21 will describe in writing, years before that reunion's own ambush makes it literal.

The granary district was never built to be defended -- it was built to feed people, and the same silos that stored the capital's own surplus turn out to store just as much for whatever the synod is running further in. Holding it isn't victory, just a delay.

'The synod's colossus is fed from here' turns out to be exactly as literal as it sounds -- a body assembled from what the granary quietly diverted, standing where a district used to be one thing and is now becoming another. Whether this is the same hunger the Idol and the Hierophant answer to, or just the capital's own version of it, is not a question this fight settles.
